newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nintendo mulls boosting N64 game shipments to U.S. [CORRECTED 08:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Nintendo mulls boosting N64 game shipments to U.S. [CORRECTED 08:40 GMT]

text.p: Nintendo Co Ltd said on Thursday it is considering boosting shipments of its N64 video game players to the United States in view of their popularity there.

Nintendo's unit in the United States, Nintendo of America, said on Wednesday that its entire shipment of new N64 video game machines, totalling 350,000 units, sold out at retail stores three days after their launch.
N64, known as Nintendo 64 in Japan, boasts improved graphics and is faster than the the older system which uses 16-bit chips.
"We were told the U.S. wants at least 1.5 million units of N64 by the Christmas season," a Nintendo executive said.
Nintendo initially planned to ship 1.4 million units to overseas markets by the end of March 1997 (corrects from March 1996).
